rows.Clause / Topic: Employer free-issue reinforcement steel delay - primary TIA clause
rows.Location: Clause 4.20 / Appendix advance payment steel supply / Clause 8.4 / Clause 20.1
rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer-supplied or client supplied reinforcement steel is tied to the approved programme and advance-payment arrangement. Late, short, or unusable free-issue steel can support a Delay TIA only when the Contractor proves timely requisition, readiness to use the steel, and critical path impact.
rows.Research the Lines: Priority keywords: steel, reinforcement, RFT, free issue, employer supplied, client supplied, material shortage, approved programme, requisition, delivery notes, stock records, activity impacts, critical path, TIA, EOT. This should rank first for steel shortage events. The Contractor position is strongest where the affected activity was ready, predecessors were complete, and the delay window is measured from stock-out/need date to usable recovery.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor has leverage on time if records prove readiness and criticality; Employer has leverage if requisitions, readiness, or critical path are weak.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate notice under Clause 20.1 and monthly claim account required. State activity ID, required steel date, requested quantity, delivered quantity, shortage, affected programme update, and intended TIA fragnet.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation, disruption, and steel/concrete price adjustment only if non-Contractor delay and no uncompensable concurrency are proven.
rows.Schedule Impact: Strong EOT candidate if the stock-out delays a critical or longest-path activity, consumes float, or delays a contractual milestone after proper TIA insertion.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved baseline/update programme; steel requisitions; delivery notes; stock ledger; material inspection records; activity readiness proof; predecessor completion; photos; daily reports; CPM/TIA fragnet; concurrency review; notice and monthly claim updates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: The 25 percent advance includes a steel-supply component, with 70 percent as steel supplied by the Employer according to the approved programme.
rows.Research the Lines: This links free-issue steel to payment and programme administration. It does not by itself prove delay; it proves the source of supply and makes approved programme dates, requisitions, and delivery records central evidence.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify immediately when steel supply under the advance mechanism is late, short, or not usable against approved programme needs.
rows.Money Impact: Affects advance/payment reconciliation and may support prolongation or escalation only when delay responsibility is established.
rows.Schedule Impact: Supports causation for free-issue steel delay if the affected activity was ready and impacted the critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved programme; advance-payment terms; steel delivery schedule; requisitions; receipts; delivery notes; shortage calculations; balance curve; correspondence requesting recovery commitments.

rows.Clause / Topic: Extension of Time entitlement and TIA proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: EOT is available only for qualifying Employer/Engineer risk events that delay completion or a contractual milestone and are claimed under the notice procedure.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this row for all Delay TIA conclusions. A valid event needs cause, effect, critical path/float impact, contemporaneous notice, and an update-impact/TIA calculation. Simple addition of delay days is not enough.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor if critical path proof and notice are strong; Employer if delay is non-critical, concurrent, or unsupported.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict Clause 20.1 notice, particulars, updates, and monthly claim account. Missing or late notices create high time-bar risk.
rows.Money Impact: EOT protects from delay damages. Prolongation cost requires separate entitlement, causation, and concurrency proof.
rows.Schedule Impact: Primary schedule entitlement route for steel, RFI, IFC, access, variation, and suspension events.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Delay event register; notice register; impacted update; baseline/update schedules; fragnet logic; narrative; float path comparison; milestone impact; concurrency matrix; mitigation records.

rows.Clause / Topic: Clause 20.1 claim notice and time bar control
rows.Plain English Meaning: Failure to submit timely notice, particulars, and monthly claim updates can waive or severely weaken time and money claims.
rows.Research the Lines: This is the highest-risk defence against every otherwise valid claim. The Delay TIA engine should treat notice compliance as a gating issue, not an administrative afterthought.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor has complete notice trail
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate protective notice; detailed particulars when available; repeat in monthly claim/variation account until resolved.
rows.Money Impact: Missed notice can defeat prolongation cost, disruption cost, variation recovery, and interest arguments.
rows.Schedule Impact: Missed notice can defeat or weaken EOT even where the technical schedule impact exists.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Notice letters; submission receipts; Engineer/Employer acknowledgements; monthly claim account; updated particulars; claim register; evidence index; responsible-party chronology.

rows.Clause / Topic: Delayed drawings, IFC revisions and Engineer instructions
rows.Plain English Meaning: Late drawings, delayed instructions, design revisions, or IFC conflicts may be Employer/Engineer risk when they stop approvals, procurement, inspection, or construction activities.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this for IFC conflict, revised structural drawings, missing information, delayed approvals, and RFI response delay. Entitlement depends on request date, required-by date, late response date, actual workface impact, and critical path effect.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify once information is late or revision impact is known; identify affected activities and required response date.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation or variation cost if the revision changes scope or causes non-concurrent delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if late information delays critical design approval, procurement, inspection, or construction sequence.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI/submittal logs; drawing register; transmittals; revision clouds; response dates; approval workflow; impacted activities; predecessor/successor logic; TIA fragnet; notice letters.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Late responses to RFIs, shop drawings, material approvals, or technical submittals can become a delay event where the response was required before work could proceed.
rows.Research the Lines: The key is not merely that an RFI was late; prove the answer was needed for a specific activity and that no reasonable alternate workfront avoided the impact.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit notice when response exceeds contractual/reasonable review period and affects planned work.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost only if delay is Employer/Engineer risk and not concurrent with Contractor delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT where delayed response blocks critical or near-critical successor work.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI register; submittal register; submission/reply dates; required-by date; affected activity ID; blocked workfront records; consultant comments; programme update; mitigation attempts.

rows.Clause / Topic: Programme requirements and critical path proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: The programme must be a proper CPM/P6 programme with logic, resources/cost/cash-flow where required, and regular updates. Delay claims depend on accepted programme logic.
rows.Research the Lines: The Delay TIA is only as strong as the schedule data. Float, longest path, predecessors, successors, calendars, progress status, and data date must be traceable.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer if programme is missing, unapproved, or logic is weak; Contractor if statused updates are complete.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit/revise programmes and narratives on time; include delay impacts in monthly reporting and claim accounts.
rows.Money Impact: Weak programme proof weakens prolongation and disruption claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical path and EOT proof depends on accepted/current logic and statused update windows.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Baseline programme; update schedules; XER/PDF exports; calendars; logic report; longest-path report; float report; progress narrative; recovery plans; TIA insertion files.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Concurrent Employer and Contractor delays may allow time relief but can block or reduce money recovery for the concurrent period.
rows.Research the Lines: The concurrency matrix must split Employer delay, Contractor delay, neutral delay, and overlapping windows. Do not double count days. Separate entitlement to time from entitlement to cost.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer on money; Contractor may retain time protection if critical Employer delay is proven.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notice still required for each Employer-risk event and each updated impact period.
rows.Money Impact: No or reduced prolongation cost during true concurrency unless contract/legal position supports apportionment.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT for net critical delay, subject to causation and notice.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Concurrency matrix; event windows; responsible party coding; critical path comparison; float consumption; contractor delay register; mitigation records; narrative explaining net impact.

rows.Clause / Topic: Employer free-issue reinforcement steel delay - primary TIA clause
rows.Location: Clause 4.20 / Appendix advance payment steel supply / Clause 8.4 / Clause 20.1
rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer-supplied or client supplied reinforcement steel is tied to the approved programme and advance-payment arrangement. Late, short, or unusable free-issue steel can support a Delay TIA only when the Contractor proves timely requisition, readiness to use the steel, and critical path impact.
rows.Research the Lines: Priority keywords: steel, reinforcement, RFT, free issue, employer supplied, client supplied, material shortage, approved programme, requisition, delivery notes, stock records, activity impacts, critical path, TIA, EOT. This should rank first for steel shortage events. The Contractor position is strongest where the affected activity was ready, predecessors were complete, and the delay window is measured from stock-out/need date to usable recovery.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor has leverage on time if records prove readiness and criticality; Employer has leverage if requisitions, readiness, or critical path are weak.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate notice under Clause 20.1 and monthly claim account required. State activity ID, required steel date, requested quantity, delivered quantity, shortage, affected programme update, and intended TIA fragnet.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation, disruption, and steel/concrete price adjustment only if non-Contractor delay and no uncompensable concurrency are proven.
rows.Schedule Impact: Strong EOT candidate if the stock-out delays a critical or longest-path activity, consumes float, or delays a contractual milestone after proper TIA insertion.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved baseline/update programme; steel requisitions; delivery notes; stock ledger; material inspection records; activity readiness proof; predecessor completion; photos; daily reports; CPM/TIA fragnet; concurrency review; notice and monthly claim updates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: The 25 percent advance includes a steel-supply component, with 70 percent as steel supplied by the Employer according to the approved programme.
rows.Research the Lines: This links free-issue steel to payment and programme administration. It does not by itself prove delay; it proves the source of supply and makes approved programme dates, requisitions, and delivery records central evidence.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify immediately when steel supply under the advance mechanism is late, short, or not usable against approved programme needs.
rows.Money Impact: Affects advance/payment reconciliation and may support prolongation or escalation only when delay responsibility is established.
rows.Schedule Impact: Supports causation for free-issue steel delay if the affected activity was ready and impacted the critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved programme; advance-payment terms; steel delivery schedule; requisitions; receipts; delivery notes; shortage calculations; balance curve; correspondence requesting recovery commitments.

rows.Clause / Topic: Extension of Time entitlement and TIA proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: EOT is available only for qualifying Employer/Engineer risk events that delay completion or a contractual milestone and are claimed under the notice procedure.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this row for all Delay TIA conclusions. A valid event needs cause, effect, critical path/float impact, contemporaneous notice, and an update-impact/TIA calculation. Simple addition of delay days is not enough.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor if critical path proof and notice are strong; Employer if delay is non-critical, concurrent, or unsupported.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict Clause 20.1 notice, particulars, updates, and monthly claim account. Missing or late notices create high time-bar risk.
rows.Money Impact: EOT protects from delay damages. Prolongation cost requires separate entitlement, causation, and concurrency proof.
rows.Schedule Impact: Primary schedule entitlement route for steel, RFI, IFC, access, variation, and suspension events.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Delay event register; notice register; impacted update; baseline/update schedules; fragnet logic; narrative; float path comparison; milestone impact; concurrency matrix; mitigation records.

rows.Clause / Topic: Clause 20.1 claim notice and time bar control
rows.Plain English Meaning: Failure to submit timely notice, particulars, and monthly claim updates can waive or severely weaken time and money claims.
rows.Research the Lines: This is the highest-risk defence against every otherwise valid claim. The Delay TIA engine should treat notice compliance as a gating issue, not an administrative afterthought.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor has complete notice trail
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate protective notice; detailed particulars when available; repeat in monthly claim/variation account until resolved.
rows.Money Impact: Missed notice can defeat prolongation cost, disruption cost, variation recovery, and interest arguments.
rows.Schedule Impact: Missed notice can defeat or weaken EOT even where the technical schedule impact exists.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Notice letters; submission receipts; Engineer/Employer acknowledgements; monthly claim account; updated particulars; claim register; evidence index; responsible-party chronology.

rows.Clause / Topic: Delayed drawings, IFC revisions and Engineer instructions
rows.Plain English Meaning: Late drawings, delayed instructions, design revisions, or IFC conflicts may be Employer/Engineer risk when they stop approvals, procurement, inspection, or construction activities.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this for IFC conflict, revised structural drawings, missing information, delayed approvals, and RFI response delay. Entitlement depends on request date, required-by date, late response date, actual workface impact, and critical path effect.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify once information is late or revision impact is known; identify affected activities and required response date.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation or variation cost if the revision changes scope or causes non-concurrent delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if late information delays critical design approval, procurement, inspection, or construction sequence.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI/submittal logs; drawing register; transmittals; revision clouds; response dates; approval workflow; impacted activities; predecessor/successor logic; TIA fragnet; notice letters.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Late responses to RFIs, shop drawings, material approvals, or technical submittals can become a delay event where the response was required before work could proceed.
rows.Research the Lines: The key is not merely that an RFI was late; prove the answer was needed for a specific activity and that no reasonable alternate workfront avoided the impact.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit notice when response exceeds contractual/reasonable review period and affects planned work.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost only if delay is Employer/Engineer risk and not concurrent with Contractor delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT where delayed response blocks critical or near-critical successor work.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI register; submittal register; submission/reply dates; required-by date; affected activity ID; blocked workfront records; consultant comments; programme update; mitigation attempts.

rows.Clause / Topic: Programme requirements and critical path proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: The programme must be a proper CPM/P6 programme with logic, resources/cost/cash-flow where required, and regular updates. Delay claims depend on accepted programme logic.
rows.Research the Lines: The Delay TIA is only as strong as the schedule data. Float, longest path, predecessors, successors, calendars, progress status, and data date must be traceable.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer if programme is missing, unapproved, or logic is weak; Contractor if statused updates are complete.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit/revise programmes and narratives on time; include delay impacts in monthly reporting and claim accounts.
rows.Money Impact: Weak programme proof weakens prolongation and disruption claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical path and EOT proof depends on accepted/current logic and statused update windows.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Baseline programme; update schedules; XER/PDF exports; calendars; logic report; longest-path report; float report; progress narrative; recovery plans; TIA insertion files.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Concurrent Employer and Contractor delays may allow time relief but can block or reduce money recovery for the concurrent period.
rows.Research the Lines: The concurrency matrix must split Employer delay, Contractor delay, neutral delay, and overlapping windows. Do not double count days. Separate entitlement to time from entitlement to cost.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer on money; Contractor may retain time protection if critical Employer delay is proven.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notice still required for each Employer-risk event and each updated impact period.
rows.Money Impact: No or reduced prolongation cost during true concurrency unless contract/legal position supports apportionment.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT for net critical delay, subject to causation and notice.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Concurrency matrix; event windows; responsible party coding; critical path comparison; float consumption; contractor delay register; mitigation records; narrative explaining net impact.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Payment entitlement depends on complete monthly statements, certification, and the contractual payment period. Late payment arguments require proof of valid submission and due date.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this for IPC delay, cash-flow stress, interest, and payment-related disruption. Payment delay is not automatically an EOT event unless a contractual suspension/right or proven critical resource impact exists.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer until submission completeness and due date are proven; Contractor if certified amounts remain unpaid beyond the period.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify late/non-payment with invoice, certification, receipt date, due date, amount, and contractual interest calculation.
rows.Money Impact: Potential unpaid balance, interest, financing/prolongation argument, or suspension-related cost subject to contract compliance.
rows.Schedule Impact: Indirect only unless non-payment demonstrably caused resource demobilization, suspension, or critical productivity loss.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: IPC submission; Engineer receipt; certified amount; payment due date; cheque/cash receipt; bank records; ageing table; resource impact records; notice of non-payment.

rows.Clause / Topic: Monthly statements and material on site
rows.Plain English Meaning: Monthly statements include executed work and approved delivered materials/plants where conditions are satisfied.
rows.Research the Lines: Material on site can support cash flow but must be approved, delivered, protected, insured/owned as required, and allocated to BOQ/payment items.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit complete monthly statement with supporting material records.
rows.Money Impact: Incomplete documents delay certification/payment; complete material records improve recovery.
rows.Schedule Impact: Indirect schedule relevance through cash-flow and material availability only.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Delivery notes; MIRs; invoices; photos; storage records; insurance/ownership records; BOQ allocation; monthly valuation backup.

rows.Clause / Topic: Variation instruction and changed scope procedure
rows.Plain English Meaning: Changes require instruction/approval and timely proposal or claim procedure. A variation can support time and money only when scope change, instruction, and impact are recorded.
rows.Research the Lines: Backfilling, revised drawings, omitted/added works, access changes, and authority-driven changes should be routed through the variation register and monthly claim account.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Give notice/proposal promptly and repeat open variation in monthly account.
rows.Money Impact: Preserves valuation of extra work, changed quantities, preliminaries, and prolongation where applicable.
rows.Schedule Impact: Preserves EOT if the variation affects critical path or consumes float.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Instruction; drawing revision; VO register; quotation; cost build-up; BOQ comparison; programme impact; site records; monthly account entry.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contract documents must be read together and priority rules govern conflicts. Ambiguities must be notified and clarified.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this for drawing/specification conflicts, inconsistent BOQ/drawing scope, and IFC/RFI issues. The claim needs a clear ambiguity, timely notice, and reliance/impact proof.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify ambiguity/discrepancy immediately and request instruction before affected work proceeds where practical.
rows.Money Impact: Potential variation/payment only if clarification changes scope or causes extra cost outside existing obligation.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if clarification delay or changed requirement affects critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Conflicting documents; priority analysis; RFI; Engineer instruction; revised drawing; impact register; affected quantities; schedule fragment.

rows.Clause / Topic: Site access, possession and workfront availability
rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer or third-party access constraints can be compensable/excusable only when the Contractor proves the workfront was required, ready, and unavailable.
rows.Research the Lines: Access claims fail when Contractor had other available workfaces or predecessor constraints. Link the obstruction to the activity logic and critical path.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify access obstruction immediately with location, activity, required date, and photos.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation/disruption if Employer-risk and not concurrent.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if blocked access delays critical/near-critical work.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Handover records; access permits; photos; daily reports; affected activity IDs; alternate workfront analysis; correspondence; TIA fragment.

rows.Clause / Topic: Permits, authorities, utilities and dewatering exclusions
rows.Plain English Meaning: Some permits, utilities relocation/protection, dewatering, and Employer/Engineer site mobilization items are excluded or Employer-linked depending on facts and instructions.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this when delay is caused by authority, utility, dewatering, or excluded employer obligation. Must distinguish excluded scope from Contractor coordination obligations.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Contractor if exclusion/instruction is clear; Employer if coordination was Contractor obligation.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify as soon as authority/utility/dewatering issue affects work and request instruction.
rows.Money Impact: Potential additional payment if excluded from contract amount or instructed as extra.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if critical path affected and not Contractor-caused.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Permit correspondence; authority letters; utility drawings; site photos; instructions; cost records; programme impact; mitigation log.

rows.Plain English Meaning: The contract is re-measured and payment follows actual executed quantities, but BOQ quantity differences alone do not automatically create a claim.
rows.Research the Lines: Quantity growth becomes a time/money claim only if it is outside normal remeasurement, instructed as change, or affects critical path beyond tender risk.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify material quantity/time impact when the issue exceeds normal measurement administration.
rows.Money Impact: Payment follows measured work; extra entitlement needs measurement records and clause basis.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT only if quantity growth delays critical path and is not Contractor risk.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Survey sheets; IR approvals; quantity take-off; BOQ comparison; drawings; measurement sheets; progress records; schedule impact.

rows.Clause / Topic: Fixed price, no BOQ warranty and escalation limits
rows.Plain English Meaning: The accepted amount is fixed/final and the Employer gives no BOQ quantity warranty, except specific concrete/steel adjustment mechanisms.
rows.Research the Lines: This is an Employer defence against general escalation and quantity surprise claims. Keep steel/concrete price adjustment separate from delay/EOT entitlement.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Use the allowed price-adjustment procedure and claim notices where delay/responsibility is involved.
rows.Money Impact: Blocks broad inflation claims; may allow concrete/steel CAPMAS adjustment if conditions are met.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct EOT from price movement; only linked delay events matter.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: CAPMAS indices; baseline prices; procurement dates; delay responsibility; BOQ/drawing comparison; notice; calculation workbook.

rows.Clause / Topic: Rate of progress and recovery plan
rows.Plain English Meaning: If progress is too slow, the Contractor may need to revise methods, add resources, or submit recovery plans.
rows.Research the Lines: Employer may use this against EOT if delay is caused by poor productivity, lack of resources, or failure to mitigate. Contractor should separate Employer-risk events from own recovery obligations.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor shows external critical delay and reasonable mitigation.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Recovery notices and revised programmes should be answered with cause analysis and reservation of rights.
rows.Money Impact: Acceleration/recovery at Contractor cost if Contractor-caused; potential cost claim only if instructed acceleration after Employer delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Recovery plan affects forecast completion and mitigation narrative.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Progress S-curves; manpower/equipment histograms; recovery programme; cause coding; mitigation records; correspondence reserving rights.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Completion dates and milestones create delay-damages exposure unless EOT is granted for qualifying delays.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this to quantify management risk: EOT is both entitlement and defence against delay damages. Milestone delay needs separate activity-to-milestone traceability.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer if no EOT; Contractor if EOT proof is strong.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: EOT notices must be submitted before/when milestone exposure becomes apparent.
rows.Money Impact: Delay damages exposure and prolongation-cost defence are central commercial issues.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical milestone and completion-date impact must be shown by TIA and updated programme.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Milestone register; delay damages clause; critical path to milestone; EOT notices; impacted update; recovery and mitigation records.

rows.Clause / Topic: Suspension by Employer or non-payment response
rows.Plain English Meaning: Suspension or reduced progress rights are clause-sensitive and require strict notice and procedural compliance.
rows.Research the Lines: Do not treat cash-flow stress as automatic delay entitlement. If suspension/non-payment route is used, prove contractual trigger, notice, waiting period, and actual critical impact.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor strictly follows procedure.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Formal notice before suspension/slowdown and continued updates after impact.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost/time if valid suspension; high rejection risk if procedure missed.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT only for properly invoked suspension or proven critical resource impact.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Payment due notices; unpaid certificates; suspension notices; resource records; productivity records; programme impact; mitigation alternatives.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Force majeure applies only to exceptional events meeting the contract definition and procedural notice requirements.
rows.Research the Lines: Not a default route for ordinary supply, payment, design, or coordination delays. Use only where event is external, unavoidable, and contractually qualifying.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict notice and mitigation records required.
rows.Money Impact: Usually limited; depends on contract wording.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT for qualifying event if critical path impacted.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Event proof; authority notices; contemporaneous records; mitigation log; schedule impact; notices.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Testing, completion documents, and taking-over requirements can affect completion and handover entitlement.
rows.Research the Lines: Late approvals or failed tests can be Employer or Contractor risk depending on cause. Separate defect/rework from delayed Employer/Engineer action.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify delayed tests, inspections, or taking-over blockers promptly.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation or withheld payment depending on cause.
rows.Schedule Impact: Can affect completion milestone if on critical handover path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Inspection requests; test records; NCRs; completion checklist; as-built/submittal status; handover correspondence; programme impact.

rows.Clause / Topic: Shop drawings, as-builts, Revit and CAD deliverables
rows.Plain English Meaning: The Contractor must submit required shop drawings, as-builts, Revit/CAD source files, and technical documents in the required format and time.
rows.Research the Lines: This is both a Contractor obligation and a delay defence. Employer may reject delay if Contractor documents were late/incomplete; Contractor may claim if Engineer response or revised requirement delayed approved documents.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit early; notify delayed review or changed requirement when it affects activities.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost only for changed requirements or delayed Employer/Engineer response.
rows.Schedule Impact: Submittal approval delay can affect procurement/construction logic.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Submittal schedule; transmittals; review cycles; comments; revisions; approval dates; linked activities; delay notices.

rows.Plain English Meaning: The Contractor remains responsible for planning, coordination, resources, mitigation, and cooperation even when Employer-risk events occur.
rows.Research the Lines: Employer rebuttal usually alleges lack of readiness, poor sequencing, insufficient resources, late submittals, or failure to mitigate. Delay TIA must answer those points.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor readiness and mitigation are documented.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Reservation-of-rights notices should include mitigation steps and remaining blockers.
rows.Money Impact: Weak mitigation reduces recoverable cost.
rows.Schedule Impact: Weak mitigation can reduce or defeat EOT.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Readiness checklist; resource logs; alternate workfront analysis; mitigation plan; daily reports; correspondence; progress updates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Engineer instructions, determinations, and responses form the administrative route before disputes.
rows.Research the Lines: Requests should ask for clear instruction/determination and reserve rights. Silence or delayed determination should be recorded and escalated.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Refer claims and disputed determinations through required contractual steps.
rows.Money Impact: Determinations affect valuation, payment, and claim entitlement.
rows.Schedule Impact: Determinations affect accepted EOT and recovery obligations.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Engineer instructions; determinations; submissions; meeting minutes; claim particulars; response deadlines; escalation letters.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Disputes follow the contract?s determination and court route where no DAB process applies.
rows.Research the Lines: Keep the claim file litigation-ready: facts, notices, causation, programme analysis, quantum, and correspondence must be self-contained.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Do not skip required Engineer determination/claim procedure before dispute escalation.
rows.Money Impact: Affects recoverability and dispute strategy.
rows.Schedule Impact: Affects formal EOT recognition and delay damages defence.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Claim dossier; evidence index; chronology; clause matrix; TIA report; quantum file; meeting minutes; formal determinations.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Project is the Big Project civil works between Roya as Employer and Samco as Contractor, effective 30-Apr-2025.
rows.Research the Lines: All later letters should be read against this baseline: parties, project, price, time, and risk allocation are fixed from this date.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Use exact contract references in all notices.
rows.Money Impact: Defines the starting commercial baseline.
rows.Schedule Impact: Defines the baseline programme period.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep contract date, parties, amount, and commencement records in every claim file.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contract amount is EGP 367,286,025 including social insurance, duties, and taxes except VAT.
rows.Research the Lines: The price is intended to be comprehensive. The Contractor must prove why any extra is outside the agreed scope or qualifies under variation/adjustment clauses.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Any extra must follow Variation or Claim procedure.
rows.Money Impact: High barrier to extra payment unless clear instruction/change exists.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct time right unless linked to variation or delay event.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: For each extra cost, attach instruction, BOQ gap analysis, and timely notice.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contract is on a re-measured basis and payment is based on actual executed quantities.
rows.Research the Lines: Quantities can increase or decrease, but rates and risk wording still matter. More quantity is not automatically a new scope claim.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Measurement records must be timely and supported.
rows.Money Impact: Payment follows measured work, not tender BOQ quantity warranty.
rows.Schedule Impact: Quantity change may affect time only if it impacts critical path and is claimed.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep survey sheets, IR approvals, measurement sheets, and BOQ mapping.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer gives no warranty that BOQ quantities are accurate.
rows.Research the Lines: The Contractor cannot rely only on tender quantities to claim surprise. The claim must be tied to changed scope, instruction, or unforeseeable condition.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Claim notice still required if quantity change delays or costs more than normal remeasurement.
rows.Money Impact: Limits quantity-based claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible only if actual quantity change affects critical path and is properly proved.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Compare tender BOQ, IFC drawings, actual measurements, and programme impact.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Accepted amount is fixed and final, inclusive of compensation, contingencies, future law, fuel, and currency changes except specified material adjustment.
rows.Research the Lines: This is a strong anti-claim clause. Most market escalation arguments are blocked unless they fit the concrete/steel adjustment formula.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Use price adjustment clause only where allowed.
rows.Money Impact: Reduces escalation and hardship claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct EOT from price movement.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Separate allowed concrete/steel adjustment from general inflation claims.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Concrete and steel may be adjusted using CAPMAS indices if delay is not due to Contractor.
rows.Research the Lines: Price adjustment is conditional. If Employer/Engineer says the Contractor caused the delay, the adjustment may be rejected.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Need proof delay was not Contractor-caused.
rows.Money Impact: Potential recovery for concrete/steel escalation only.
rows.Schedule Impact: Depends on non-contractor delay period and affected procurement.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Prepare CAPMAS index comparison, baseline prices, procurement dates, and delay responsibility analysis.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer/Engineer site mobilization, authority permits/licenses, relocation/protection of utilities, and dewatering are excluded.
rows.Research the Lines: These are possible entitlement areas, but only if actually instructed or required and not already covered elsewhere.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Variation/claim notice required before or immediately after impact.
rows.Money Impact: Potential additional payment if outside scope and instructed/required.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if critical and not Contractor fault.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Record instruction, site condition, authority requirement, photographs, and cost/time impact.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Advance payment is 25 percent; 30 percent cash against bank check and 70 percent as steel supplied by Employer according to approved programme.
rows.Research the Lines: Steel supply is commercially tied to the advance. But entitlement depends on approved programme and proper requisitions.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Steel delay notices should be immediate and linked to approved programme dates.
rows.Money Impact: Employer-supplied steel affects advance/payment accounting.
rows.Schedule Impact: Late steel may support delay only if critical and properly requested.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep approved programme, steel requisitions, delivery notes, and impact analysis.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Minimum IPC amount is 70 percent of monthly cash flow.
rows.Research the Lines: Small or weak IPCs can be administratively rejected or deferred. Payment entitlement is linked to monthly cash flow planning.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Monthly IPC must meet threshold and be complete.
rows.Money Impact: Can delay cash collection if IPC below threshold.
rows.Schedule Impact: Indirect cash-flow pressure; not itself an EOT event.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Align monthly valuation with approved cash flow and explain any shortfall.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer pays amounts due within 45 days after Engineer receives a complete statement and supporting documents.
rows.Research the Lines: The 45 days likely starts only after a compliant submission, not after an incomplete invoice.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Late payment arguments need proof of complete submission date.
rows.Money Impact: Interest or delayed payment arguments depend on compliance.
rows.Schedule Impact: Suspension rights require strict clause compliance.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep transmittal, Engineer receipt date, checklist of supporting documents, and payment certificate.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Proof of social insurance payment is required before subsequent IPC release.
rows.Research the Lines: Even technically valid work may be held up if social insurance evidence is missing.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit before each affected IPC cycle.
rows.Money Impact: Payment can be delayed despite completed work.
rows.Schedule Impact: Indirect cash flow risk only.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep receipts, certificates, and IPC checklist.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Retention is 5 percent; first half released at Taking-Over Certificate and second half after Defects Notification Period.
rows.Research the Lines: Cash is locked until formal completion milestones, not just physical progress.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Taking-over and defect records must be clean.
rows.Money Impact: Cash retention affects final recovery.
rows.Schedule Impact: Open defects delay release.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Track TOC requirements, snag/NCR closure, and DNP expiry.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Performance security is 5 percent of Accepted Contract Amount.
rows.Research the Lines: Security gives Employer leverage if termination, default, or recovery of damages becomes serious.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Maintain valid security until required release.
rows.Money Impact: Potential call/deduction risk.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct schedule effect, but default pressure is high.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Track validity, expiry, amendments, and Employer notices.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Time for Completion is 19 months from Commencement Date.
rows.Research the Lines: All delay analysis should measure impact against this contractual completion window.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: EOT claim required for any excusable delay.
rows.Money Impact: Delay damages risk after expiry without EOT.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical path must be shown against 19-month baseline.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain approved baseline programme and monthly updates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Ground floor ceiling slab completion is required within 8 months from Commencement and is not a Taking-Over section.
rows.Research the Lines: This is a milestone obligation but does not give partial taking-over protection. Delay can still be used as performance evidence.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify delay to milestone if affected.
rows.Money Impact: Potential damages/pressure depending on contract use.
rows.Schedule Impact: High control milestone for early works.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Track milestone logic, progress photos, inspections, and causes of delay.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Delay damages are 1 percent of outstanding works per week or part week, capped at 10 percent of Contract Price.
rows.Research the Lines: Even part of a week counts. Employer can use this as strong pressure once completion is late without EOT.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: EOT must be claimed before delay damages crystallize.
rows.Money Impact: High exposure, capped at 10 percent.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical if no approved EOT.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Update EOT register and forecast exposure weekly.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Normal hours are 6 days per week and 8 hours per day.
rows.Research the Lines: Acceleration beyond normal hours may not be paid unless instructed or caused by an Employer-risk event and properly claimed.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Acceleration claim needs instruction or recoverable delay event.
rows.Money Impact: Overtime often Contractor cost unless entitlement proved.
rows.Schedule Impact: Recovery plans may require more resources without extra payment if Contractor delay.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Record instructions, productivity assumptions, manpower, and cause of acceleration.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contract documents are prioritized by the Agreement sequence.
rows.Research the Lines: If two documents conflict, priority decides. But the Contractor must still flag conflicts before execution.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify ambiguity before starting affected work.
rows.Money Impact: May block extra payment if Contractor proceeds silently.
rows.Schedule Impact: May block EOT if late clarification caused by Contractor silence.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain discrepancy notices and Engineer responses.

rows.Plain English Meaning: If Employer considers a more stringent requirement applicable, Contractor must comply.
rows.Research the Lines: The stricter interpretation can be imposed first, with entitlement only if Contractor preserves claim rights.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify and claim if stricter requirement changes cost/time.
rows.Money Impact: Potential extra cost only if valid variation/claim survives.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential delay only if critical and noticed.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Issue reservation letter before execution, then submit variation proposal.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Missing, unpriced, or blank BOQ items are deemed included in other BOQ rates/prices.
rows.Research the Lines: A BOQ silence is not enough to claim extra. Contractor must show the work is truly outside the Contract, not just missing from a rate.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Variation notice required for true extra scope.
rows.Money Impact: Strongly limits payment for omitted rate items.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct EOT unless scope/instruction affects critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Map work to drawings/specs and explain why it is not implied or included.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Work shown in any contract document but not another is deemed included in Accepted Contract Amount.
rows.Research the Lines: One drawing/specification reference can be enough to make the work included.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Raise discrepancy before execution.
rows.Money Impact: Extra payment difficult if item appears anywhere in contract docs.
rows.Schedule Impact: EOT difficult unless delayed instruction/change occurs.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Search all contract documents before asserting missing scope.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Works necessary for stability, completion, safe operation, or proper execution are included even if not expressly detailed.
rows.Research the Lines: The contract captures hidden enabling works. Many support, temporary, coordination, and completion items may be treated as included.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Claim only if beyond normal implied works and instructed/changed.
rows.Money Impact: Limits extras for temporary or enabling items.
rows.Schedule Impact: May create sequencing burden on Contractor.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Record why the work is unusual, instructed, or outside normal construction practice.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contractor must notify Engineer of ambiguity, discrepancy, or error before starting affected work.
rows.Research the Lines: If Contractor builds first and argues later, entitlement becomes weak.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify before work starts.
rows.Money Impact: Late notice can defeat additional cost.
rows.Schedule Impact: Late notice can defeat delay claim.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Send technical query/RFI with proposed interpretation and reservation of rights.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Submittals are due 14 days before construction activity; Engineer review is 10 days; resubmission is 3 days.
rows.Research the Lines: The programme must include approval cycles. Late submittals become Contractor delay even if Engineer takes normal review time.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Late submittal notices weaken claims.
rows.Money Impact: Rework/resubmission cost likely Contractor risk.
rows.Schedule Impact: Approval delay only claimable beyond contractual review if critical.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain submittal register tied to programme activities.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Delay from late drawings/instructions must be claimed under the notice procedure.
rows.Research the Lines: The event may be Employer-risk, but it is not automatically payable or excusable unless notice and particulars are on time.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict notice required, then particulars and monthly updates.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost/time only if claim compliant.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if critical path delayed.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep request dates, required-by dates, late response proof, and critical path analysis.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer gives site access under contract conditions.
rows.Research the Lines: Access is entitlement-sensitive: if the Contractor cannot work because access is not given, it can be strong, but only with proof of readiness and criticality.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate notice if access not available.
rows.Money Impact: Possible cost if proven and not excluded.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT if critical access denied.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep handover records, photographs, readiness evidence, and programme logic.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Authority permits/licenses are excluded from Accepted Contract Amount, but responsibilities depend on the specific permit and law.
rows.Research the Lines: This is a possible variation/claim zone, but not a blanket excuse for slow authority processing.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify authority delay and cost as soon as known.
rows.Money Impact: Recoverable if Employer-risk or excluded cost instructed/required.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT if authority issue blocks critical work and Contractor acted diligently.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep applications, authority receipts, correspondence, and delay chronology.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Engineer administers instructions and determinations under the Contract.
rows.Research the Lines: Engineer decisions are central evidence. Silence or informal site discussion is weaker than written instruction/determination.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Ask for written instruction/determination where impact exists.
rows.Money Impact: Payment depends on formal valuation/determination.
rows.Schedule Impact: Delay depends on accepted programme impact.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Convert verbal directions into written confirmation immediately.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contractor must execute, complete, and remedy defects in accordance with the Contract and good practice.
rows.Research the Lines: Broad duty means Contractor carries coordination, means, methods, and completion risk unless a clause shifts it.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify only where Employer-risk event prevents performance.
rows.Money Impact: Defects/rework usually Contractor cost.
rows.Schedule Impact: Contractor-caused delay not excusable.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep method statements, approvals, inspection records, and defect closure evidence.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contractor must verify and review design documents as required by the Contract.
rows.Research the Lines: Failure to review early can make later design objections look like Contractor delay or late discovery.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Raise design issues promptly and before affected works.
rows.Money Impact: Late design comments may not justify extra cost.
rows.Schedule Impact: Late review can delay shop drawings/procurement.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain design review log, consultant reports, RFIs, and dates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contractor must cooperate with other contractors and anticipate simultaneous work.
rows.Research the Lines: Minor disruption, sequencing changes, and interface inconvenience may already be priced and programmed.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Only substantial, critical, Employer-caused interference should be claimed.
rows.Money Impact: Minor interface cost likely unrecoverable.
rows.Schedule Impact: Minor resequencing likely no EOT.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep interface meeting minutes, obstruction logs, photos, and critical path proof.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Unexpected physical conditions may support entitlement if properly notified and proven.
rows.Research the Lines: Site difficulty alone is not enough. Contractor must show unforeseeability, impact, and compliance with notice rules.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate notice before disturbing evidence where possible.
rows.Money Impact: Possible cost if conditions qualify.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT if critical path affected.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Preserve photos, survey, test reports, expert opinion, and baseline assumptions.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Utilities relocation/protection is excluded from price, but Contractor must manage site utilities obligations carefully.
rows.Research the Lines: Utility events can be claimable if outside scope, but damage or poor protection can become Contractor liability.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify conflict/damage immediately and follow variation/claim procedure.
rows.Money Impact: Potential extra for instructed protection/relocation; liability if Contractor damages utilities.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if utility issue blocks critical work and not Contractor fault.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep utility drawings, trial pit records, permits, photos, and incident reports.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer-supplied items, especially steel as part of advance, depend on approved programme and requisition process.
rows.Research the Lines: A steel delay claim needs proof that Contractor requested correctly, was ready to use it, and the delay hit critical path.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notice immediately if free issue material is late, defective, or short.
rows.Money Impact: May affect payment/advance and possible prolongation.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT if critical and not Contractor-caused.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep approved programme, requisitions, delivery notes, stock records, and activity impacts.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Daily, weekly, and monthly reports must include progress, delay analysis, programme update, logs, photos, procurement, submittals, quality, and pending issues.
rows.Research the Lines: Reports are not paperwork only. They become the project record for delay, payment, and claim proof.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Monthly claim/variation account must be separate and up to date.
rows.Money Impact: Weak reports weaken IPCs and claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: Weak reports weaken delay analysis.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Submit complete reports and reconcile them with notices, programme updates, and IPCs.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contractor must submit shop drawings, as-built drawings, and source files where required.
rows.Research the Lines: Late or incomplete drawings can stop approvals, inspections, and taking-over.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Follow submittal timing and resubmission period.
rows.Money Impact: Rework/correction generally Contractor cost.
rows.Schedule Impact: Can become Contractor delay if on critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain drawing register, revision history, approvals, and transmittals.

rows.Plain English Meaning: If Contractor fails to submit or obtain approval of QMS, Employer/RFP quality plan may be deemed final.
rows.Research the Lines: Contractor loses control over the quality framework if its own plan is late or rejected.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: QMS details due early after commencement.
rows.Money Impact: Noncompliance can lead to rejected work and withheld approvals.
rows.Schedule Impact: Rejected IRs/NCRs can delay progress and taking-over.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Submit QMS, QC manager approval, ITPs, NCR logs, and corrective action records.

rows.Plain English Meaning: If Contractor fails to submit or approve HSE plan, Employer/RFP safety plan may govern.
rows.Research the Lines: Safety noncompliance can stop work and still remain Contractor risk.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit HSE plan and incident reports on time.
rows.Money Impact: Stop-work or corrective measures may be Contractor cost.
rows.Schedule Impact: Safety stoppages can delay works without EOT if Contractor fault.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep HSE plan, inductions, toolbox talks, PPE logs, accident reports, and close-outs.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Key Contractor personnel require approval and compliance with contract requirements.
rows.Research the Lines: Changing or lacking approved staff can be treated as management noncompliance and used against progress claims.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify changes and obtain approvals.
rows.Money Impact: May affect payment/certification indirectly.
rows.Schedule Impact: Weak staffing undermines EOT defenses.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep CV approvals, org chart, attendance, and replacement approvals.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Programme must be P6, resource/cost/cash loaded, with narratives, long lead items, free issue materials, and other contractors' milestones.
rows.Research the Lines: A simple bar chart is not enough. Without a compliant baseline/update, delay claims become much harder to prove.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Programme submission and monthly update deadlines matter.
rows.Money Impact: IPC, cash flow, and delay claims depend on programme quality.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical path proof depends on accepted logic.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep baseline, updates, narratives, calendars, resources, cash flow, and change logs.

rows.Plain English Meaning: If delay reaches 10 percent of remaining calendar days or at least 45 days, Contractor must submit recovery plan within 28 days.
rows.Research the Lines: The contract creates an early warning and acceleration pressure mechanism before final delay damages.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Recovery plan due within 28 days after update showing delay.
rows.Money Impact: Recovery may be Contractor cost if delay is Contractor risk.
rows.Schedule Impact: Failure worsens delay exposure.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Submit recovery plan with manpower, shifts, resequencing, procurement, and float recovery.

rows.Plain English Meaning: EOT is available only for qualifying events and compliant claims.
rows.Research the Lines: Even a real Employer-caused delay can be lost if notice, particulars, monthly updates, or critical path proof are missing.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict claim notice and monthly account requirements.
rows.Money Impact: Prolongation cost depends on entitlement and concurrency rules.
rows.Schedule Impact: EOT protects against delay damages if proven.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain delay event register, notices, particulars, updates, and delay analysis.

rows.Plain English Meaning: If progress is too slow, Contractor may be required to revise methods or accelerate.
rows.Research the Lines: If the delay is Contractor-caused, recovery is usually at Contractor cost.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Respond quickly to slow-progress notices.
rows.Money Impact: Additional resources may not be payable.
rows.Schedule Impact: Recovery obligations can change sequence and productivity.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep productivity records and separate Contractor delay from Employer delay.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Engineer/Employer may instruct suspension under contract conditions.
rows.Research the Lines: Suspension can be entitlement-bearing if not Contractor fault, but must be documented precisely.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notice/claim immediately after suspension instruction and resumption.
rows.Money Impact: Possible cost if compensable under contract.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT if critical path affected.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep suspension instruction, affected resources, idle plant/labour, and restart records.

rows.Clause / Topic: Tests on completion and failed tests
rows.Plain English Meaning: Failure to pass tests can trigger remedial obligations and retesting.
rows.Research the Lines: Testing failure usually shifts time/cost risk back to Contractor unless caused by Employer design/instruction.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify cause if failure not Contractor fault.
rows.Money Impact: Retesting/remedial cost likely Contractor risk.
rows.Schedule Impact: Failed tests delay taking-over.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep test plans, results, calibration, causes, corrective works, and retest approvals.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Taking-over requires substantial completion and conditions such as no rejected IRs, no open NCRs, clear site limits, debris removal, and safe access.
rows.Research the Lines: Physical completion is not enough. Paperwork, NCRs, housekeeping, and safe access can block TOC and retention release.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Apply for TOC only with supporting close-out evidence.
rows.Money Impact: Retention release and final payment depend on TOC.
rows.Schedule Impact: Delay damages risk continues until TOC/completion accepted.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Prepare TOC dossier, NCR closeout, as-builts, test certificates, and site clearance evidence.

rows.Plain English Meaning: DNP is 365 days and Contractor must remedy defects.
rows.Research the Lines: The project is not commercially finished at TOC. Defects affect final retention and final certificate.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Respond to defect notices promptly.
rows.Money Impact: Unremedied defects may be deducted or completed by others.
rows.Schedule Impact: Defects can delay final release.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Maintain defect register, response dates, repair records, and Engineer acceptance.
